sources.quote: Either borrowed from Polish witać, from Proto-Slavic *vitati or arose as a reanalyzation of приві́т (pryvít) "hello, hi" → приві́тати (pryvítaty) → віта́ти (vitáty), in which case came from Proto-Slavic *větъ "agreement". Doublet of вита́ти (vytáty, “soar, dwell”).

sources.quote: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic житиѥ (žitije, “life”), from Proto-Slavic *žitьje, from Proto-Slavic *žiti (“to live”). Doublet of життя́ (žyttjá), the inherited East Slavic form.
